articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities and Individuals for Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Activities
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on November 13, 2026, targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics and counter terrorism activities.
These designations aim to disrupt financial networks supporting illicit drug trafficking and terrorist organizations globally, reinforcing U.S. national security objectives.
Further details regarding the specific individuals and entities, and the nature of their illicit activities, are available on the Treasury's website.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran Designation Update
body: OFAC released an update to its Iran designations on November 9, 2026, modifying existing listings related to the Iranian sanctions program.
This update reflects ongoing efforts to refine and strengthen sanctions against entities and individuals supporting the Iranian regime's destabilizing activities.
The specific changes in the designation update can be found on the official OFAC recent actions page.

articles.headline: New Iran-Related Designations Announced by OFAC
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) imposed new Iran-related designations on November 6, 2026, targeting additional individuals and entities.
These actions are part of a broader strategy to exert economic pressure on Iran in response to its nuclear program and support for regional proxy groups.
The Treasury Department's announcement provides detailed information on the newly sanctioned parties and the reasons for their designation.

articles.headline: OFAC Targets Cyber-related and Transnational Criminal Organizations, Issues Cuba Designations and Determination
body: OFAC announced a series of designations on November 5, 2026, focusing on cyber-related threats and transnational criminal organizations, alongside new designations related to Cuba.
The actions against cyber and criminal groups aim to disrupt their financial infrastructure and prevent illicit activities that pose a threat to U.S. national security and economic stability.
Additionally, OFAC published a Cuba-related determination, further clarifying the scope of sanctions against the Cuban regime.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Iran-Related Designations, Updates Listings, and Amends Venezuela General License
body: On November 4, 2026, OFAC announced new Iran-related designations and provided updates to existing Iran-related listings.
Concurrently, the agency issued an amended Venezuela-related General License and a corresponding Frequently Asked Question, indicating adjustments to the sanctions program concerning Venezuela.
An Iran-related OFAC Alert was also published, providing guidance and highlighting potential risks associated with transactions involving Iran.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Iran-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an amended Iran-related General License on October 29, 2026.
This amendment provides updated guidance and authorizations for certain transactions involving Iran, reflecting ongoing adjustments to the sanctions regime.
The specific details of the amended General License are available on the OFAC website for public review.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities in North Korea and Democratic Republic of the Congo
body: OFAC announced new designations on October 28, 2026, targeting entities in North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
These actions aim to counter illicit activities, including proliferation financing and human rights abuses, in both regions.
The designations underscore the U.S. commitment to addressing threats to international peace and security.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Filing Reports
body: On October 26, 2026, OFAC issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) regarding blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC.
These updates provide clarifications and additional guidance for financial institutions and other entities on their compliance obligations under OFAC regulations.
The revised FAQs are an important resource for ensuring proper adherence to sanctions requirements.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Settles with OFAC for $1,529,685

The settlement resolves alleged violations of OFAC sanctions programs.
Further details of the violations and the terms of the settlement are outlined in the enforcement release.

This determination follows the removal from the Entity List of Arrow China Electronics Trading Co., Ltd., and the removal of six aliases for Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. in November 2025.

articles.headline: Removal From the Entity List

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
